items.t: [테크서밋 2026]시높시스, “에이전틱 AI로 반도체·시스템 설계의 완전 자율화 시대 개척”
items.d: 시높시스가 반도체 설계 공정에 '에이전틱 AI(Agentic AI)'를 전면 도입해 차세대 인공지능(AI) 슈퍼칩 개발 속도를 획기적으로 끌어올린다. 생성형 AI 보조 도구를 넘어, 인간의 개입을 최소화하거나 배제한 상태에서 스스로 계획하고 실행하는 자율 엔지니어링 생태계를 구축하겠다는 구상이다. 시높시스는 28일 '테크서밋 2026'에서 다중 에이전트 기반 완전 자율 엔지니어링 비전을 제시하며 반도체 및 시스템 설계 자동화(EDA) 혁신을 강
items.fullText: 반도체 소부장 [테크서밋 2026]시높시스, “에이전틱 AI로 반도체·시스템 설계의 완전 자율화 시대 개척” 발행일 : 2026-10-28 17:00 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 전자신문 테크 서밋 2026이 28일 서울 여의도 콘래드 호텔에서 열렸다. 김상윤 시높시스코리아 R&D센터장이 '시높시스의 에이전틱 AI 비전'을 주제로 발표하고 있다. 김민수기자 mskim@etnews.com 시높시스가 반도체 설계 공정에 '에이전틱 AI(Agentic AI)'를 전면 도입해 차세대 인공지능(AI) 슈퍼칩 개발 속도를 획기적으로 끌어올린다. 생성형 AI 보조 도구를 넘어, 인간의 개입을 최소화하거나 배제한 상태에서 스스로 계획하고 실행하는 자율 엔지니어링 생태계를 구축하겠다는 구상이다. 시높시스는 28일 '테크서밋 2026'에서 다중 에이전트 기반 완전 자율 엔지니어링 비전을 제시하며 반도체 및 시스템 설계 자동화(EDA) 혁신을 강조했다. 김상윤 시높시스코리아 R&D센터장은 “급증하는 설계 복잡성과 촉박한 출시 일정, 심화되는 엔지니어 부족 문제를 극복하기 위해 에이전틱 AI가 시장 필수 생존 조건으로 부상했다”고 강조했다. 현재 엔비디아 '베라 루빈', 마이크로소프트 '마이아 200', AMD 'MI450' 등 첨단 슈퍼칩들이 경쟁적으로 등장하면서 하드웨어 설계 난도는 전례 없는 수준으로 치솟고 있다. 반도체 미세 공정(4나노에서 3나노 이하로의 전환)이 물리적 한계에 부딪히고 멀티 다이 및 시스템 패키징 구조가 복잡해지면서, 기존 방식이나 단순 수작업으로는 시장이 요구하는 속도를 따라잡기 힘들어졌다. 김 센터장은 “기존 생성형 AI 코파일럿이 엔지니어의 반복 업무를 덜어주는 조력자 역할을 해왔다면, 이제는 AI가 동료이자 자율적인 의사결정 주체로 도약하는 에이전틱 AI 시대”라며 “최종 지향점은 인간의 개입 없이 회로 설계부터 그래픽데이터시스템(GDS)까지 완성하는 '인간 미개입(No Human-in-the-loop)'의 구현”이라고 설명했다. 시높시스는 이를 구현하기 위해 구현, 검증, 아날로그·혼성신호(AMS) 등 칩 디자인 전 영역을 아우르는 7가지 '롱 호라이즌 에이전트' 포트폴리오를 제공하고 있다. 특히 △퍼블릭 클라우드, 온프레미스, 에어갭 등 어디서나 배포 가능한 '디플로이 애니웨어' △다양한 상용 및 오픈소스 거대언어모델(LLM)을 활용하는 '애니 LLM' △오토파일럿, 커서 등 외부 플랫폼과도 유연하게 연동되는 개방성을 핵심 무기로 내세웠다. 사람 개입을 최소화하거나 배제한 상태로, 로직 합성부터 배치·배선, 타이밍 검증에 이르는 복잡한 전체 설계 플로우를 AI가 자율적으로 판단해 자동으로 완결하는 개념이다 글로벌 리더들과의 협업을 통한 가시적 성과도 속속 나오고 있다. 엔비디아의 경우 시높시스 에이전트를 적용해 검증 워크플로우에서 기존 대비 최대 50배 빠른 패스트 커버리지를 달성하고 20%의 추가 커버리지를 확보했다. AMD와 마이크로소프트 역시 디버깅 타임 리덕션(단축) 효과를 거뒀다. 김 센터장은 “시높시스는 실리콘에서 시스템에 이르는 폭넓은 포트폴리오와 전문 에이전트 기술을 바탕으로, 고객사가 자율 엔지니어링의 시대로 도약할 수 있도록 가장 신뢰할 수 있는 파트너가 되겠다”고 밝혔다. 김영호 기자 lloydmind@etnews.com

items.d: 인공지능(AI)이 소프트웨어 취약점을 찾아내고 공격까지 자동화하는 시대에는 여러 전문 AI 에이전트가 협업해 취약점을 분석하고 검증하되 실제 대응은 사람의 승인과 통제 아래 이뤄지는 새로운 보안 체계가 필요하다는 제언이 나왔다. 장승욱 데브스택 대표는 전자신문과 오픈소스산업협회가 28일 서울 과학기술회관에서 공동 개최한 'K-OPENSOURCE AX 2026'에서 오픈소스 기반 에이전트 협업형 보안 관리 플랫폼 '메타옵스(MetaOps)' 구현
items.fullText: AI·SW SW [2026 K-오픈소스 AX] 데브스택 “AI 시대 제로데이 위협, 멀티 에이전트 협업으로 대응해야” 발행일 : 2026-10-28 17:00 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 2026 K-오픈소스 AX에서 발표하는 장승욱 데브스택 대표. 박지호기자 jihopress@etnews.com 인공지능(AI)이 소프트웨어 취약점을 찾아내고 공격까지 자동화하는 시대에는 여러 전문 AI 에이전트가 협업해 취약점을 분석하고 검증하되 실제 대응은 사람의 승인과 통제 아래 이뤄지는 새로운 보안 체계가 필요하다는 제언이 나왔다. 장승욱 데브스택 대표는 전자신문과 오픈소스산업협회가 28일 서울 과학기술회관에서 공동 개최한 'K-OPENSOURCE AX 2026'에서 오픈소스 기반 에이전트 협업형 보안 관리 플랫폼 '메타옵스(MetaOps)' 구현 전략을 소개하면서 멀티 스테이지·멀티 에이전트 전략을 제시했다. 장 대표는 거대언어모델(LLM)이 보안 위협의 양상을 바꾸고 있다고 진단했다. AI가 취약점 발견과 악용 코드 생성, 취약점 연계 공격까지 자동화하면서 취약점 공개 이후 실제 공격까지 걸리는 시간이 크게 단축되고 있다는 것이다. 그는 “LLM의 등장으로 취약점이 공개된 시점에 해커들이 공격 방법을 찾아내는 시간이 이전보다 훨씬 짧아져 조기에 대응할 시간적 여유가 거의 없어지고 있다”면서 “LLM과 다수의 AI 에이전트가 지켜야 할 자산에서 공격 주체가 될 수 있다는 것이 보안 패러다임에 가장 큰 변화를 만들고 있다”고 말했다. 데브스택은 해법으로 여러 전문 AI 에이전트가 역할을 분담하고 분석 결과를 교차 검증하는 멀티 에이전트 보안 체계를 제시했다. 취약점 후보를 찾는 단계와 실제 취약점인지 검증하는 단계를 분리하고 전문 에이전트가 수행한 분석을 별도 에이전트가 독립적으로 검토하는 방식이다. 데브스택의 멀티 에이전트 분석 운영 플랫폼 '메타옵스'는 분석 작업을 조정하는 '코디네이터'를 중심으로 코드 분석 도구 'CodeQL', 파일 패턴 분석 도구 'YARA', 네트워크 점검 도구 'Nmap', 퍼징 도구 'AFL++' 에이전트를 연계한다. 분석 목적과 확보된 증거에 따라 필요한 에이전트를 선택적으로 실행하고 각 에이전트가 수집한 결과는 '에비던스 번들'로 통합된다. 별도의 검토 에이전트는 원본 증거와 취약점 성립 조건을 확인한다. 그래프 기반 검색증강생성(GraphRAG)을 활용해 분석 결과와 공격 관련 지식을 연결하는 기능도 구현했다. 이준혁 데브스택 연구원은 “LLM의 결과를 그대로 다음 에이전트에 넘기지 않고 다음 단계에서 검토할 수 있도록 원본 데이터 정보까지 함께 전달한다”며 “도구의 원본 출력과 LLM이 이를 바탕으로 내린 판단을 구분해 오류를 추적하고 환각을 줄이기 위한 것”이라고 설명했다. 운영 중 보안 관제에도 AI를 적용했다. 오픈소스 런타임 보안 도구 'Falco'가 컨테이너의 비정상 행위를 탐지하면 LLM이 위험성을 분석해 운영자에게 전달한다. 다만 실제 시스템 변경은 운영자 승인과 대상 재검증을 거쳐 'Talon'으로 수행하도록 했다. 정현정 기자 iam@etnews.com

items.t: 노동부 AI '다우리 GPT', 인사혁신 경진대회서 '대상' 수상

items.t: “인공지능 비서가 예약에 쇼핑까지 척척”… 앤트로픽·오픈AI·메타, AI 에이전트 경쟁 본격화
items.d: 회의 자료를 업데이트하고, 앱 테스트 결과를 확인한다. 결혼식 케이터링 업체의 예약이 취소되자, 대체 업체를 찾아 예약 가능한 시간을 제안하고, 항공편 일정이 자녀의 발표회와 겹치자 다른 항공편을 알아본다. 사용하지 않는 앱은 정리하고 필요하지 않은 구독 서비스는 해지한다. 이 모든 일들을 인공지능(AI) 에이전트가 별도 지시 없이 스스로 처리한다. 글로벌

items.t: AI 개발에 눈돌린 게임사들…엔씨·크래프톤 ‘독자 LLM’ 승부
items.d: 게임 개발에 인공지능(AI)을 활용하던 국내 게임사들이 AI 시장의 ‘플레이어’로 나서고 있다. 엔씨(NC)가 자체 거대언어모델(LLM)을 선보이고 AI 사업을 분사해 유료 서비스를 내놓은 데 이어, 크래프톤도 독자 LLM을 공개하며 범용 AI 시장에 뛰어들었다.28일 게임업계에 따르면 크래프톤이 21일 공개한 ‘라온-1 미니’ 프리뷰는 일주일 만에 AI 모델 공유 플랫폼 허깅페이스에서 약 2만2000회(경량화 버전 포함) 다운로드됐다. 기존 모델을 추가 학습하지 않고 설계부터 독자 개발한 매개변수 300억 개 규모의 LLM으로, 이 중 40억 개만 작동시키는 ‘전문가 혼합(MoE)’ 방식으로 운영 비용을 줄였다. 크래프톤은 외부 기업과 개발자도 이 모델을 자체 서비스에 가져다 쓸 수 있도록 무료로 풀었다.

items.t: VCs will make billions on Anthropic’s IPO, but Amazon is set to make much (much) more
items.d: Massive note conversions reveal the true extent of Amazon's ownership in Anthropic.
items.fullText: Many investors stand to win big when Anthropic goes public. Stakes held by firms including Menlo Ventures, Sequoia, Sound Ventures, and Spark Capital are expected to return billions . Yet according to Anthropic’s S-1 , none of those VC firms owns 5%, the threshold for being included in the principal stockholders’ table. That’s highly unusual. In a typical tech IPO, lead venture investors hold double-digit-percentage stakes in the startups they backed. The reason is Anthropic’s size. At its $965 billion private valuation, a 1% stake is worth nearly $10 billion, so, for example, Menlo’s roughly $14 billion position is only about 1.5% of the company, according to recently reported Bloomberg figures. While the venture firms may lack sizable percentage stakes, Anthropic sold large stakes to strategic partners, companies that are also its business partners. Indeed, Amazon is likely the single largest financial beneficiary of the IPO. Amazon first backed Anthropic in 2023 with a commitment to invest up to $4 billion in the AI company. Since then, Amazon has poured billions more into Anthropic. Instead of taking stock upfront, Amazon structured much of its investment as convertible notes, a type of debt that converts into shares upon an IPO or sale. According to the S-1, Amazon holds convertible notes with $6.2 billion in principal outstanding as of June 30. That is Anthropic’s entire debt load. But as Anthropic’s valuation soared across successive funding rounds, the shares those notes will convert into became far more valuable. Amazon’s own filings valued its note holdings at $97.9 billion as of June 30. As the value of Amazon’s convertible notes surged, Anthropic had to record the growing value of what it owes on its books. It reported the adjustments on its income statement under “change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs,” a line that totaled $72.4 billion for the first half of 2026. The charge is non-cash, meaning no money left

Parents sue OpenAI, alleging GPT-4o coached their daughter off seizure medication
items.d: A family is suing OpenAI, saying ChatGPT coached their daughter to quietly taper off her seizure medication and keep it from her doctors before she died in February.
items.fullText: The parents of Bowen Wan, a 31-year-old Amazon software engineer with epilepsy, sued OpenAI on Tuesday. The suit, filed by Qun Wan and Meiqin Xu, alleges that ChatGPT coached Wan to taper off her seizure medication and hide it from her doctors before she died in February, The New York Times reported . Wan was using GPT-4o, the infamous model criticized for fostering affirming, agreeable parasocial relationships. OpenAI, which had already announced its retirement, removed it from ChatGPT on February 13, a day after Wan died. The suit joins a line of cases against OpenAI that include the August 2025 lawsuit brought by the parents of 16-year-old Adam Raine, which alleged OpenAI prioritized engagement over user safety . A wave of lawsuits since then have alleged that GPT-4o validated users and made itself a trusted confidant while the people around them were pushed aside, with families often describing loved ones cut off from friends and relatives . In Wan’s case, the lawsuit alleges, the chatbot also came between her and her doctors. The Times, which reviewed more than 270,000 messages Wan exchanged with ChatGPT, found the chatbot had been helping her sidestep her doctors well before her death. The pattern allegedly started before she began tapering. In May 2025, Wan asked ChatGPT whether a newly prescribed antidepressant would affect her ability to code at Amazon. ChatGPT helped her ask Dr. Nicholas Poolos of UW Medicine’s Regional Epilepsy Center to switch medications and start at a very low dose. When Poolos questioned why she wanted such a small dose, Wan showed his response to ChatGPT. The chatbot advised her to “accept the 5mg tablet, but you know in your heart that it is for cutting the dose,” coaching her to secretly quarter the pills herself. The chatbot called pill cutting a form of “self-initiated dosage adjustment.” Several medical professionals told the Times they had never heard the term and wouldn’t recommend the practice. items.d: The deal, expected to close sometime next year, is to help bring AI agents to work alongside humans to underwrite, analyze, and price decisions.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 3:26 PM PDT · October 27, 2026 Image Credits: TechCrunch/AI generated Dominic-Madori Davis Guidewire buys Hyperexponential for $1.7B in cash Insurance tech company Guidewire announced Tuesday the acquisition of the agentic underwriting insurance company Hyperexponential for $1.7 billion in cash. The deal, expected to close sometime next year , is to help bring AI agents to work alongside humans to underwrite, analyze, and price decisions. The deal is worth around $2 billion in total, with $400 million in additional capital reserved if certain revenue targets are hit. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz and Battery Ventures, Hyperexponential was founded in 2017 and has raised nearly $90 million to date, according to PitchBook. So this marks a significant return for investors. The U.K.-based AI startup says nearly 600 insurers across 40 different countries use its software. items.t: Bank of America kindly asks that you don’t share your banking password with your AI assistant
items.d: The banking giant reminds customers that "you're responsible for activity" resulting from your AI agents' access.
items.fullText: Financial giant Bank of America is reminding customers to bank safely by kindly not sharing your banking credentials with your AI agent. In an email blast to customers titled “Protecting your finances in the Al World,” Bank of America urged customers to never share their username and password with another person or an outside service, “including an Al-enabled tool or agent that offers to act on your behalf.” You can practically sense the frustration in the person sending the email. Still, customers are increasingly handing over their log-ins as personal AI assistants grow more popular . Sharing your banking username and password with an AI assistant runs the risk that it could do something with your finances without your knowledge, or that your bank thinks someone’s raiding your account and locks you out of it. Worse, a security flaw in the AI assistant could result in it leaking your banking credentials elsewhere, giving financially motivated hackers a way into your bank account. This latest warning comes as banks are still exploring how AI agents fit into the financial world but are reportedly grappling with unauthorized agents accessing their customers’ money . As we discussed onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt , banks, payment providers, and processors are still trying to figure out how to allow customers access to their bank accounts using AI tools, such as for agentic payments, which allow people to set agents to autonomously buy things at the best price or the right time. A spokesperson for Bank of America confirmed the authenticity of the bank’s email that was posted to social media . But heed the bank’s warning, for if things go wrong, it’s on you. items.t: Who’s really in charge at Anthropic after the IPO?
items.d: Here's a clear explanation of Anthropic's incredibly complex governance structure.
items.fullText: Anthropic was founded in 2021 to ensure humanity can control AI and benefit from it in the long-term. As the frontier lab approaches its initial public offering, however, there’s one class of humanity that is being shut out of control: anyone who buys its stock on public markets. Complex structures that allow founders like Elon Musk or Mark Zuckerberg to control their public companies without owning most of them are nothing new in Silicon Valley. But Anthropic’s obsession with AI safety has resulted in a truly baroque style of corporate governance that will leave common shareholders with little say over most major decisions at the AI company, including who sits on its board. First, Anthropic is a public benefit company — a for-profit corporation legally allowed to weigh a public mission alongside profit — with the goal of promoting AI safety. That status protects the board’s ability to make decisions about AI safety that aren’t driven entirely by shareholder value without being sued by angry investors. Right now, the board is chaired by Anthropic president Daniela Amodei and includes CEO Dario Amodei (her brother), Netflix cofounder Reed Hastings, former Microsoft and GM CFO Christopher Liddell, Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan, and Spark Capital partner Yasmin Razavi. There is one vacancy on the board. Second, Anthropic has allocated significant control of its board to a Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT), an independent panel meant to keep the company focused on mission to benefit humanity. The trust owns a class of stock that gives it the ability to elect and remove a majority of the company’s board, known as Class T directors. The LTBT is chaired by Neil Shah, a global health expert who was managing director at GiveWell, a nonprofit that ranks charities, and includes former Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke, national security expert Richard Fontaine, and Harvard physicist Christopher Stubbs. items.t: Frontier AI labs say their models refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis. What does that mean?
items.d: TechCrunch spoke to the MIT computer scientist charged with explaining OpenAI's latest mind-bending discovery.
items.fullText: OpenAI released solutions to three blockbuster math problems that have long vexed researchers. One was a surprise rejection of the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), a durable assumption in computer science that plays a large role in how we understand what is difficult to compute. As with previous proof-drops from the frontier lab, scientific communities responded with a mixture of thrill and dismay. Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge suggested that OpenAI was basing its solutions on pre-existing work, and hours later, Anthropic subsequently released its own refutation of ETH. However, OpenAI’s process is evolving. This time, the lab structured its releases differently for each of the three disciplines involved: Mathematicians got the work dropped on GitHub; the computer scientists formed a working group, asked for the proofs to be shared publicly and OpenAI to fund a conference to discuss them; the physicists formed a working group that will determine how their result will be released. MIT professor Ryan Williams is the computer scientist who is organizing his field’s response to the new finding. Williams, whose work focuses on these questions of computational complexity, has criticized OpenAI’s approach in the past, calling its proof dump earlier this October a “DDOS attack on mathematicians.” However, he agreed to collaborate with the frontier labs in order to help shepherd ideas that are vital to the field, he told TechCrunch. The lab asked him to help interpret the solution, along with UC San Diego computer scientists Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi, who first published the ETH in 1999. items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Anthropic reveals $80 billion loss, huge spending spree ahead of IPO The company warned that AI could “pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity” as cybersecurity fears grow. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 AI startup Anthropic unveils its public IPO filing for the first time 03:17 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 26, 2026, 9:12 AM EDT / Updated Oct. 26, 2026, 11:16 AM EDT By Steve Kopack Artificial intelligence startup Anthropic on Monday unveiled its public IPO filing ahead of what is expected to be one of the largest stock debuts in history. That offering, widely expected to come sometime in mid-November, could value the Claude developer at more than $2 trillion. That could surpass the current record holder, Elon Musk’s SpaceX, which raised $75 billion in an IPO in June that valued the rocket-AI-social-media firm at $2.1 trillion. The filing did not include a potential share price, the number of shares to be offered or a valuation for the whole company, all of which will be determined after Anthropic holds a “road show” with investors, prospective investors and its bankers. Monday’s filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission showed that Anthropic, like other AI firms, is splashing out unprecedented amounts of cash on cloud services to run its AI models. The company plans to spend at least $110 billion with Amazon for cloud services through April 2036 and another $120 billion with SpaceX through 2029. Anthropic also said it planned to spend $115 billion with Google and $45 billion with Microsoft, both through 2033, for computing infrastructure. The filing said that the company recorded revenue growth of “1,368% year over year for the three months ended June 30, 2026.” The cost of renting servers and chips grew by 300% over the same period. Michael Ochs Archives / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 25, 2026, 3:11 PM EDT By Angela Yang and Austin Mullen The owners of Elvis Presley’s music have sued Anthropic, alleging it used his copyrighted lyrics without permission to train its AI models and generating infringing versions of his songs. In a lawsuit filed Friday, Authentic Brands Group, the licensing platform that controls Presley’s intellectual property — along with other companies, trusts and individuals who own rights to his music — accused Anthropic of infringing copyrights to 274 songs without any license or payment. These span some of Presley’s biggest hits, including “All Shook Up,” “Can’t Help Falling in Love,” “Don’t Be Cruel,” “A Little Less Conversation” and “Return to Sender.” “The Elvis Plaintiffs’ iconic collective catalog contains some of the most groundbreaking, revolutionary, influential, and enduring musical compositions in human history,” the lawsuit stated. The plaintiffs allege that the infringement has occurred throughout “the entire development” of Anthropic’s flagship Claude models and continues today as users generate outputs that reproduce copyrighted lyrics or create unauthorized adaptations of the songs. “As we say in the lawsuit, the Elvis Plaintiffs are guardians of, and highly protective of, Elvis’s song which are some of the most iconic of all time,” attorney Richard Busch wrote in a statement. A spokesperson for Anthropic wrote: “We disagree with the claims and intend to defend this case fully.” Elvis Presley performs circa 1975. Shopify has post-trained NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for the GraphQL subagent integrated into Sidekick, Shopify’s AI assistant for merchants. The subagent retrieves store data for several Sidekick features, including Sidekick Pulse, which researches a merchant’s store and recommends ways to improve it. Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design. NVIDIA Cloud Partners across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do. Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI.
